items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We got to be good friends from that point on, close friends. We had a lot of high respect for one another. We played together quite a few times too.

ctx.x: From that point on, we chatted for a while. I got his address – New York address. I called him. We got to be good friends from that point on, close friends. We had a lot of high respect for one another. We played together quite a few times too.

Let’s got back and talk about the rest of that triumvirate. We already talked about Papa Jo, Big Sid, and Chick Webb. Now we have the Gene, Louie, and Buddy. So talk about your first meeting with Gene Krupa. Here you are. You’re playing with Benny Goodman. Gene’s the one who really made that chair. So what was it like to meet him for the first time?

items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: like starting with Chick Webb, Big Sid Catlett, Jo Jones, Buddy, Gene, Elvin Jones, Tony Williams, Shelly Manne and Steve Gadd

ctx.x: You’ve got it covered. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -14-

But you know it’s great fun when you’re doing something that you really love to do, it’s a lot of fun, and as long as I can keep doing it I’ll be hitting rim shots and crashing cymbals. Oh yeah, I got a new CD now that was just released on Concord, and I’ve always wanted to do this, it’s a salute honoring twelve great drummers, most of them from the back era and some are in the present state, and a few that are still living, like starting with Chick Webb, Big Sid Catlett, Jo Jones, Buddy, Gene, Elvin Jones, Tony…
Oh, boy, that’s quite a project, to try to capture all the —
